notes.text: Available in cPanel 74 and later for the selected cPanel account. The pinned source declares x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none, including retrieval functions; this method uses form POST. The client performs one request with no automatic retry or rollback.

Deploys changes from the selected cPanel-managed repository. Deployment requires a valid checked-in .cpanel.yml in the top-level directory, one or more local or remote branches, and a clean working tree. Pulling uses --ff-only: HEAD must already be up to date or capable of fast-forwarding. Failed prerequisites disable deployment functionality and hide deployment information.

The response fields are optional. deploy_id is a string here, while retrieve returns integer deploy_id. timestamps.queued is a string and preserves its fractional timestamp spelling. Task IDs, log paths and SSE URLs are payload data; request success does not establish deployment completion and the client does not follow or poll them.

Deletes the deployment task identified by the supplied deployId string. This operation is distinct from deleting a repository; it does not claim to undo a deployment. Empty strings and the string 0 are forwarded unchanged.

The pinned nullable object has no field schema. Preserve opaque object fields and explicit null; an absent data member is a payload mismatch. Existing empty-object compatibility also accepts an empty JSON list, but not a nonempty list.

Retrieves deployment-task status for the selected account. The pinned source still declares x-readonly=false, so this retrieval retains form POST. Deployment requires a checked-in top-level .cpanel.yml, branches and a clean working tree; otherwise the server hides deployment information and disables deployment functionality.

All row fields are optional. deploy_id is an integer here, unlike the string returned by create. repository_state.date is an integer Unix timestamp; active, canceled, failed, queued and succeeded timestamps are strings. A status timestamp is returned only when that state occurred according to the pinned source. Preserve omission and string precision; do not invent nullable fields.

Task IDs, log paths and SSE URLs remain payload data. Request success means the status request succeeded, not that deployment succeeded; inspect task state separately. The client performs no polling, log reads or SSE connections.
